42963-the-weird-orient-nine-mystic-tales.description: A book by Henry Iliowizi. Iliowizi has hitherto contributed principally to the literature of his race, being known among Jews by several works; most widely, perhaps, by a volume of stories of Russian life, under the title of "In the Pale," recently published by the Jewish Publication Society of America for its subscribers.

arxiv-1903-11893.title: Integrable Modifications of the Ito–Narita–Bogoyavlensky Equation
arxiv-1903-11893.creator: Rustem N. GARIFULLIN and Ravil I. YAMILOV
arxiv-1903-11893.description: Abstract We consider five-point differential-difference equations. Our aim is to find integrable modifications of the Ito–Narita–Bogoyavlensky equation related to it by non-invertible discrete transformations. We enumerate all modifications associated to transformations of the first, second and third orders. As far as we know, such a classification problem is solved for the first time in the discrete case.

arxiv-2103-06904.description: Abstract . Let h h be a harmonic function defined on a spherical disk. It is shown that Δ k ​ | h | 2 \Delta^{k}|h|^{2} is nonnegative for all k ∈ ℕ k\in\mathbb{N} where Δ \Delta is the Laplace-Beltrami operator.

arxiv-2107-01659.title: Time Series Graphical Lasso and Sparse VAR Estimation
arxiv-2107-01659.creator: Aramayis Dallakyan Rakheon Kim Mohsen Pourahmadi Texas A&M University
arxiv-2107-01659.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aramayis Dallakyan Rakheon Kim Mohsen Pourahmadi Texas A&M University. Abstract

We improve upon the two-stage sparse vector autoregression (sVAR) method in
Davis et al. 2016
by proposing an alternative two-stage modified sVAR method which relies on time series graphical lasso to estimate sparse inverse spectral density in the first stage, and the second stage refines non-zero entries of the AR coefficient matrices using a false discovery rate (FDR) procedure.

arxiv-2309-00047.title: Dynamic-ADAPT-QAOA: An algorithm with shallow and noise-resilient circuits
arxiv-2309-00047.creator: Nikola Yanakiev, Normann Mertig, Christopher K. Long, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
arxiv-2309-00047.description: Abstract The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is an appealing proposal to solve NP problems on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. Making NISQ implementations of the QAOA resilient to noise requires short ansatz circuits with as few CNOT gates as possible. Here, we present Dynamic-ADAPT-QAOA.

arxiv-2410-09324.title: Token Pruning using a Lightweight Background Aware Vision Transformer
arxiv-2410-09324.creator: Sudhakar Sah, Ravish Kumar, Honnesh Rohmetra, Ehsan Saboori
arxiv-2410-09324.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sudhakar Sah, Ravish Kumar, Honnesh Rohmetra, Ehsan Saboori. High runtime memory and high latency puts significant constraint on Vision Transformer training and inference, especially on edge devices. Token pruning reduces the number of input tokens to the ViT based on importance criteria of each token. We present a Background Aware Vision Transformer (BAViT) model, a pre-processing block to object detection models like DETR/YOLOS aimed to reduce runtime memory and increase throughput by using a novel approach to identify background tokens in the image.

arxiv-2412-00619.title: Floquet Chern Vector Topological Insulators in Three Dimensions
arxiv-2412-00619.creator: Fangyuan Ma, Junrong Feng, Feng Li, Ying Wu, Di Zhou
arxiv-2412-00619.description: Abstract We theoretically and numerically investigate Chern vector insulators and topological surface states in a three-dimensional lattice, based on phase-delayed temporal-periodic interactions within the tight-binding model. These Floquet interactions break time-reversal symmetry, effectively inducing a gauge field analogous to magnetic flux. This gauge field results in Chern numbers in all spatial dimensions, collectively forming the Chern vector.

pmc-10589834.title: Evaluation of a Portable Blood Gas Analyzer for Prehospital Triage in Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Instrument Validation Study
pmc-10589834.creator: Matthieu Lyon, Christophe Alain Fehlmann, Marc Augsburger, Thomas Schaller, Catherine Zimmermann-Ivol, Julien Celi, Birgit Andrea Gartner, Nicolas Lorenzon, François Sarasin, Laurent Suppan, Amaryllis Mavragani, Alexandre Allonneau
pmc-10589834.description: BackgroundCarbon monoxide (CO) poisoning is an important cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Symptoms are mostly aspecific, making it hard to identify, and its diagnosis is usually made through blood gas analysis. However, the bulkiness of gas analyzers prevents them from being used at the scene of the incident, thereby leading to the unnecessary transport and admission of many patients.

pmc-10745397.title: The Combination of Upconversion Nanoparticles and Perovskite Quantum Dots with Temperature-Dependent Emission Colors for Dual-Mode Anti-Counterfeiting Applications
pmc-10745397.creator: Qun Zhang, Yuefeng Gao, Lihong Cheng, You Li, Sai Xu, Baojiu Chen, Elias Stathatos
pmc-10745397.description: Novel and high-security anti-counterfeiting technology has always been the focus of attention and research. This work proposes a nanocomposite combination of upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) and perovskite quantum dots (PeQDs) to achieve color-adjustable dual-mode luminescence anti-counterfeiting. Firstly, a series of NaGdF4: Yb/Tm UCNPs with different sizes were synthesized, and their thermal-enhanced upconversion luminescence performances were investigated.

pmc-11421694.title: Direct observation of degassing during decompression of basaltic magma
pmc-11421694.creator: Barbara Bonechi, Margherita Polacci, Fabio Arzilli, Giuseppe La Spina, Jean-Louis Hazemann, Richard A. Brooker, Robert Atwood, Sebastian Marussi, Peter D. Lee, Roy A. Wogelius, Jonathan Fellowes, Mike R. Burton
pmc-11421694.description: Transitions in eruptive style during volcanic eruptions strongly depend on how easily gas and magma decouple during ascent. Stronger gas-melt coupling favors highly explosive eruptions, whereas weaker coupling promotes lava fountaining and lava flows. The mechanisms producing these transitions are still poorly understood because of a lack of direct observations of bubble dynamics under natural magmatic conditions.

pmc-11565705.title: Potential of Fiber and Probiotics to Fight Against the Effects of PhIP + DSS-Induced Carcinogenic Process of the Large Intestine
pmc-11565705.creator: Aida Zapico, Nuria Salazar, Silvia Arboleya, Carmen González del Rey, Elena Diaz, Ana Alonso, Miguel Gueimonde, Clara G. de los Reyes-Gavilán, Celestino Gonzalez, Sonia González
pmc-11565705.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We determined the in vivo counteracting effect of fiber and probiotic supplementation on colonic mucosal damage and alterations in gut microbiota caused by 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo [4,5-b] pyridine (PhIP) and sodium dextran sulfate (DSS). Male Fischer-344 rats were randomly divided into 4 groups: control (standard diet), PhIP + DSS group (standard diet + PhIP + DSS), fiber (fiber diet + PhIP + DSS), and probiotic (probiotic diet + PhIP + DSS).

pmc-12618848.title: JAK inhibitors in the management of extra-intestinal manifestations in inflammatory bowel disease
pmc-12618848.creator: Fotios S Fousekis, André Jefremow, Konstantinos H Katsanos, Markus F Neurath, Raja Atreya
pmc-12618848.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Extra-intestinal manifestations (EIMs) commonly occur in patients with inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) and contribute significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Their management remains challenging. Recently, the development of Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitors has expanded the therapeutic options of luminal IBD, and three JAK inhibitors, tofacitinib, upadacitinib, and filgotinib, have been approved for IBD treatment, while a growing body of evidence suggests that JAK inhibitors may be a promising therapeutic option for the management of EIMs, particularly those affecting the joints

pmc-12626162.title: Sebetralstat for On‐Demand Treatment of Mucosal Hereditary Angioedema Attacks in KONFIDENT‐S
pmc-12626162.creator: Jonathan A Bernstein, Emel Aygören‐Pürsün, Mauro Cancian, Danny M Cohn, Timothy Craig, Vesna Grivcheva‐Panovska, Anthony Jordan, William R Lumry, Inmaculada Martinez‐Saguer, Isaac Melamed, Kazumasa Ohmura, Jonny Peter, Marc A Riedl, Daniel F Soteres, Petra Staubach, Marcin Stobiecki, Ya‐Hsiu Chuang,
pmc-12626162.description: BackgroundHereditary angioedema (HAE‐C1INH) attacks involving mucosal tissue may progress rapidly and often lead to substantial morbidity. Severe laryngeal attacks can be fatal without prompt administration of on‐demand treatment. This prespecified interim analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of sebetralstat in laryngeal and abdominal attacks in the ongoing, 2‐year, open‐label extension KONFIDENT‐S study (NCT05505916).

pmc-12934340.title: Beetroot juice supplementation enhances the effects of blood flow restriction training on lower limb strength and vertical jump performance under fatigue in male university students: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
pmc-12934340.creator: Xudong Yang, Yue Lu, Sang Ki Lee, Hongqi Xu, Hualong Chang, Qing Liu, Helong Quan
pmc-12934340.description: BackgroundBeetroot juice (BRJ) supplementation has the potential to enhance the effects of blood flow restriction (BFR) training in improving muscle strength and fatigue resistance; however, evidence supporting their combined effects remains limited. This study investigated whether BRJ supplementation enhances the effects of BFR training on muscle strength and fatigue resistance.

pmc-13265658.title: Effects of working memory and reward reactivity on externalizing behaviors in the ABCD study
pmc-13265658.creator: Elana Schettini, Jennifer Cheavens, Zeynep M. Saygin
pmc-13265658.description: Deficits in working memory and reward reactivity may contribute to behavioral dysregulation. Using behavioral and neural data from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD 5.1) study, we examined associations among biological systems, environmental risk, and childhood externalizing behaviors (i.e., aggression, rule breaking). Behavioral measures included List Sorting and Cash Choice tasks to assess working memory and reward processing, respectively.

pmc-13272988.title: Unchanged prevalence and increased severity of anemia from 2019 to 2022 in emergency care outpatients: A cross-sectional study from a tertiary care university hospital of Pécs, Hungary
pmc-13272988.creator: Zsuzsanna Faust, Margit Solymár, Enikő Nemes-Nagy, Sándor Pál, Hussain Alizadeh, Péter Kanizsai, Boglárka Finta, Veronika Dolmán, Nelli Farkas, Barbara Réger, Attila Miseta
pmc-13272988.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the prevalence of anemia in Hungary between 2019 and 2022 as detailed data in this regard was not available.MethodsThis retrospective, observational, cross-sectional study enrolled 85628 patients with a median age of 63 (44-76 interquartile range) years admitted to the Emergency Department of the University of Pécs, Hungary, between January, 2019, and December, 2022.

pmc-13462958.title: Intelligent financial forecasting using transformers, neuro-symbolic AI, and agent-based systems
pmc-13462958.creator: V. Jeyajeev, R. Jagadeesh Kannan, R. Deebalakshmi, Balaji Ganesh Rajagopal, V. Jeyakrishnan, Mohamed Abbas, Shaeen Kalathil
pmc-13462958.description: Forecasting the stock market is a difficult task because of the volatile price movements and complex temporal dependencies. Established models frequently do not realize these unstable trends, which leads to changeable forecasting. This paper introduces a comfortable AI-driven framework that incorporates a sequence-to-prediction transformer model with LLM-based decision-making for accurate and understandable stock price prediction.

pmc-13536075.title: Implementation and evaluation of a quality improvement initiative for central venous catheter management in neonates undergoing therapeutic hypothermia for perinatal asphyxia
pmc-13536075.creator: Margreet R Koolen-De Koninck, Tom Ouwehand, Florian Cassel, Sinno HP Simons, Gerbrich E van den Bosch
pmc-13536075.description: ObjectivesTherapeutic hypothermia (TH) is an effective treatment for hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy in infants following perinatal asphyxia, reducing mortality and morbidity when initiated within 6 hours after birth. Both perinatal asphyxia and TH require intensive management and therefore central venous access, such as umbilical venous catheters (UVC) or peripherally inserted central catheters (PICC).

pmc-13680057.title: Exploring the Connection of Otitis Media with Effusion and Allergic Rhinitis: A Systematic Review
pmc-13680057.creator: Álef Lamark Alves Bezerra, Gabriela Brill Ney, Fayez Bahmad Jr
pmc-13680057.description: Introduction Otitis media with effusion (OME) is characterized by fluid accumulation in the middle ear behind an intact eardrum, often coexisting with allergic rhinitis, an inflammatory nasal condition causing symptoms such as nasal obstruction. Both conditions are prevalent in children and may share immune-mediated mechanisms linked to the unified airway concept.
